prompt: By the lesson, which two things decide how large a decision document should be?
hint: Look at the axes of the chart.

choices.text: Whether the company has a template for it
choices.why: A template answers how to write it, not how large it should be.

choices.text: How senior the author is
choices.why: Seniority changes nothing about who will be surprised by the outcome.

choices.text: How many teams it touches and how hard it is to undo
choices.why: Right: a cheap change in one team needs a message; a hard-to-undo change across teams needs a proposal or an RFC.

choices.text: How many engineer-weeks the change will take
choices.why: Effort matters to the cost block, but a cheap change can still bind every team.

prompt: Two engineers agree in a chat thread to change the format of an event other teams consume. What test from the lesson says the decision needed a document?
hint: Who finds out when it breaks?

choices.text: Whether somebody outside the conversation will be surprised
choices.why: Right: the consuming teams were not in the chat and will find out when something of theirs breaks.

choices.text: Whether a manager was online when they agreed and could have objected
choices.why: Authority does not inform the people who will live with the change.

choices.text: Whether the chat thread ran past fifty messages
choices.why: A long thread is a sign of disagreement, which is a different problem.

choices.text: Whether the change is more than a hundred lines of code
choices.why: Size of the diff is not the test; a one-line format change can break three teams.

prompt: What does the Amazon practice described in the lesson remove from a meeting?

choices.text: The discussion, since the memo is read aloud and settles the matter
choices.why: Discussion starts after the reading; the memo informs it.

choices.text: Half the room reading it for the first time as the author talks
choices.why: Right: everybody reads it in silence first, so the discussion starts from the same page.

choices.text: The author, who is not in the room while the memo is read
choices.why: Nothing in the practice removes the author.

choices.text: The need for anybody to prepare anything
choices.why: The opposite: somebody writes up to six pages before the meeting.

prompt: Put the blocks of a one-pager in the lesson's order.
hint: Each answers the question left by the one above.
items: The title, which is the decision
The ask, with the decider and the date
What happens if we do nothing

prompt: Why does the lesson insist on the "if we do nothing" block?
hint: It changes what kind of request the page is.

choices.text: It turns a request for approval into a decision
choices.why: Right: without it, the decider weighs the cost against nothing.

choices.text: It frightens the decider into saying yes quickly
choices.why: Lívia's states the trend and the worse case plainly; its job is to inform, not to frighten.

choices.text: It is where the author lists the alternatives that were rejected
choices.why: Options belong in a proposal; the one-pager only links to them.

choices.text: It is required by the company template
choices.why: The lesson argues for it on its own merits, not by rule.

prompt: Henrique sends Renata a one-pager describing three designs, with no recommendation, "so she can choose freely". What does the lesson say?
hint: Two of the things a one-pager is not.

choices.text: A choice between designs is a proposal, and a one-pager recommends
choices.why: Right: options belong in a proposal, and a one-pager recommends.

choices.text: He should have attached the full design document instead, so she can read the detail
choices.why: That gives Renata more to read and still no recommendation.

choices.text: That is correct, because a one-pager is neutral by design and the decider chooses
choices.why: The lesson says the opposite: it recommends.

choices.text: Three designs are too many; two would be fine
choices.why: The count is not the problem; the missing recommendation is.

prompt: In Lívia's one-pager, how many reais a month does the replica cost?
Two teams ask for access to the new replica during the review. How does Lívia's proposal deal with it?

choices.text: It asks the decider to vote on it
choices.why: There is no vote; the non-goal settled it before anybody asked.

choices.text: A non-goal says "yes, later, in a separate proposal"
choices.why: Right: important, and not being decided here.

choices.text: It rejects them, because the replica is only for the route planner forever
choices.why: A non-goal is "not in this phase", not "never".

choices.text: It adds their requirements so the review can approve everything at once
choices.why: That is the scope creep non-goals exist to stop.

prompt: Why does a proposal with only one option tend to get a worse review than one with three?

choices.text: Because reviewers count the options to judge how much effort the author put in
choices.why: They judge the reasoning, which is what the alternatives expose.

choices.text: It reads as already decided, so reviewers attack it instead of checking it
choices.why: Right: shown alternatives with honest reasons turn the review into checking the reasoning.

choices.text: Because templates require at least three alternatives
choices.why: No rule; the effect is on the reviewers.

choices.text: Because one option is always the wrong one
choices.why: The single option may be right; the trouble is that nobody can see why.

prompt: Match each alternative in Lívia's proposal to the reason given about it.

pairs.right: the baseline; failures grow with volume
moves the limit rather than removing the competition
worth doing anyway, but it rations instead of separating
removes the route planner's reads from the primary

right_distractors: splits the orders database by region

prompt: A section listing what the proposal deliberately does not try to do is called the ___.
What makes a document an RFC rather than a technical proposal?
hint: The document can look the same.

choices.text: A different template, with more headings and a status line at the top
choices.why: The headings can be identical.

choices.text: Its length
choices.why: An RFC is as long as its subject; length does not define it.

choices.text: That every engineer in the company gets a vote on the outcome
choices.why: Not a vote: comments inform, one owner decides.

choices.text: Its process: a comment window, one decider, a record
choices.why: Right: the process is what lets a change affecting everybody be made without a meeting of everybody.

prompt: Put the stages of an RFC in order.
items: Open for comment until a closing date
Decision by the named owner, in writing

prompt: Marola keeps a rejected RFC about splitting the orders database by region. What does the lesson say it is worth?

choices.text: Nothing; rejected RFCs should be deleted to avoid confusion
choices.why: Deleting it is how the same week of investigation gets spent again.

choices.text: It answers "why don't we just…?" before somebody spends a week on it
choices.why: Right: the newcomer with the same idea finds the reason in ten minutes.

choices.text: It can be reopened by a vote
choices.why: RFCs are not decided by vote, and its value is in the recorded reason.

choices.text: It proves the team considered alternatives in an audit
choices.why: Possibly, but not the value the lesson names.

prompt: In what year did Steve Crocker circulate the first Request for Comments?
A proposal has been out for three weeks and Henrique, a "must review", has said nothing. What should Lívia conclude?

choices.text: That he approves
choices.why: Silence is not consent; he may not have read it.

choices.text: Nothing yet: she messages him directly
choices.why: Right: a must review who has not replied gets a direct message, not another broadcast.

choices.text: That the proposal is rejected
choices.why: Silence is no more a no than a yes.

choices.text: That he has given up his right to object
choices.why: When it breaks something of his, that argument will not help anyone.

prompt: Match each role at the top of the proposal to what it means.

pairs.right: approves or rejects by the date
comments must be answered before the decision
invited to comment; no answer needed

prompt: A comment thread between Bruna and Paulo reaches thirty replies. What does the lesson recommend?
hint: Where the disagreement is understood, and where it is written.

choices.text: Let the decider pick whoever wrote more
choices.why: Volume is not an argument.

choices.text: A short call, then the outcome written into the document
choices.why: Right: the call gets the disagreement understood quickly; the document keeps what came of it.

choices.text: Lock the comments until the closing date so the thread stops growing
choices.why: That stops the conversation without resolving it.

choices.text: Ask the whole company to vote on it in a poll
choices.why: There is no vote; a decider owns it.

prompt: Which are acceptable end states for a review comment, by the lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three states, and one of them is not here.

choices.text: Resolved silently, without a reply
choices.why: A comment that disappears unanswered teaches the reviewer to stop reviewing.

choices.text: Changed: the document now says something different
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Declined, with the reason written
choices.why: Yes: the reviewer may disagree and knows they were heard.

choices.text: Open, recorded as a question with an owner
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Lívia wants every service to get a fixed share of database connections, which all seven teams must follow. Which document?
hint: It sets a rule others must follow.

choices.text: A one-pager to Renata, since she decides budgets
choices.why: It is not a budget decision; it constrains every team.

choices.text: A chat message in the engineering channel, since it is a config change
choices.why: Small to type and binding on seven teams; the test is who will be surprised.

choices.text: A decision record with no review
choices.why: A record keeps a decision; it does not make one with the people affected.

choices.text: An RFC
choices.why: Right: it constrains all seven teams, and each knows things about its own traffic she does not.

prompt: What goes at the top of the proposal once it is decided?
hint: Two lines, for the reader a year later.

choices.text: A summary of all forty comments
choices.why: The point is that a reader should not need them.

choices.text: A new version number for the draft
choices.why: Versioning the draft does not say what was decided.

choices.text: The decision, the date, the decider and any conditions
choices.why: Right: the next reader knows what happened without the thread.

choices.text: Nothing; the decision is announced in the meeting
choices.why: Then it exists only for the people who were in the room.
